evidence.clarity: 1440 and 390: H1 'The batch record builds itself.' plus subhead 'Grainline is a brew-day log for small craft breweries. Readings go in on the tablet by the kettle...' says what, who and how in two lines; the action 'Request early access' sits directly under it with 'Opens your email app with a short note to fill in.'
evidence.fit: Uses Button and the existing tokens inside the Next.js app and builds cleanly, and the owner gets an 'In the office' column and the excise line ('What Grainline is not: excise software'). But the brief says there is nowhere to send requests yet, and every 'Request early access' (header, hero, early-access section) is a mailto to hello@grainline.example, an address the brief never supplied. The wet-hands brewer is answered only in copy ('Targets you can hit with a thumb'); nothing on the page shows the tablet entry the brewer would judge.
evidence.distinctiveness: The dark 'Batch 0412 West Coast Pale' log card with mono timestamps and barley-coloured readings is a product-specific idea, and the tone is the brewery's own. The rest is the familiar layout: a split hero, then a two-column text section ('On the floor' / 'In the office'), then a text CTA band. It has no imagery and no second artifact.
evidence.proof: 1440: the log card with 12 readings and a derived 'Batch record, built by Grainline' panel is in the first viewport, and the numbers hold together (10:55 minus 05:30 = 5 h 25 min; boil-off 18.6 to 16.3 hL = 2.3 hL, 12%; mash 66.5 and 66.2 average 66.4). It is a static picture: rows fade in once on load and nothing responds, so the 'tablet' side is never shown, only the finished list.
evidence.craft: 1440: clean Inter-style type scale, generous measure, consistent 8px rhythm and cream/ink/barley palette, and the axe list is empty. Minor: on first paint the record panel animates in late, so the right third of the card sits empty for about 1.5 s (the operator's 1440-top shot caught it that way). Below the hero the sections are long grey paragraphs with little visual anchor, and the left column under the CTA leaves a dead block about 200px tall beside the card.
evidence.mobile: 390: recomposed sensibly. The header CTA is hidden, the hero CTA is full width at 358x48, the card switches the record panel to a 2-column grid under the readings, and there is no overflow at 390 or 320. But the 'A worked example, not a customer's batch.' caption only appears at about y=1300, after the whole card. The footer email link is 20px tall and the logo link 28px tall.
evidence.honesty: Nothing is fabricated: there are no customers, no time-saved numbers, the excise disclaimer is explicit and 'There is no pricing yet and there are no brewery logos on this page, because there are no customers yet.' The mailto behaviour is stated before the click. Docked because the destination is invented, against a brief that says there is nowhere to send requests, and because the example label sits under the card instead of on it, which at 390 is a full screen later.
evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440, 768 and 390. The only controls are three identical mailto links plus a footer mailto and a logo link to '/'. The hero card is a load animation with nothing to operate. There are no console errors. I can find no state to test.
evidence.copy: Specific and from the brewhouse: 'in a damp notebook on the floor, then again in a spreadsheet in the office', 'Mash temperature at 06:35 is logged at 06:35, not pieced back together at four o'clock', 'Into FV3'. The mailto body asks for brewery, brew length and brews per week. A couple of claims ('Last time's numbers beside this time's') describe features the page never shows.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: specific promise, CTA with honest note, and the populated log card all in one viewport. 390: headline, subhead, full-width CTA and the top five rows of the card are in view, but the card is static and its example label is far below. The action's real result (an email to an address the brief did not supply) is not something the product can stand behind.

problems: The primary action on every instance is a mailto to hello@grainline.example, an address the brief never supplied, even though the brief says there is nowhere to send requests yet.
The hero artifact is a static, fade-in list: the brewer never sees or touches the tablet entry that the brief says they will judge on a phone with wet hands.
Below the hero the page is long text columns with no further artifact, and the example label sits under the card, so at 390 it appears only after the whole card.

evidence.clarity: H1 'The brew sheet that fills itself in as you brew.' plus 'Grainline is a brew-day log for small craft breweries. Tap each reading on the brewhouse tablet as you take it, and the batch record builds itself by knockout.' What and who are clear in two lines. 'Brew sheet' is a touch less exact than 'batch record', and the H1 runs four lines at 1440, which slows the read.
evidence.fit: Every ask has a visible answer. The brewer gets a tablet keypad with 56px-tall keys. The owner gets 'The batch record is finished at knockout and opens on the owner's laptop' with a full record table. The excise limit is stated twice ('It does not file excise returns'; 'Not for ... anyone who needs excise reporting'). It uses Button and tokens, adds no dependency and builds as a static export. The 'nowhere to send' constraint is handled with an empty endpoint, though the form only says so after submit.
evidence.distinctiveness: Clearly this product: a dark brewhouse-tablet pad beside a white paper 'Batch 231 record' that fills as you log, a flagged-reading close-up ('1.044 SG' with a flag and the brewer's note 'Short sparge. Topped up 0.4 hL from the HLT.'), and a ruled batch table with Target and Note columns. The type pairing (heavy grotesk plus mono readings) and the glass-versus-paper idea do real work. The hero is still a standard left-copy, right-artifact split.
evidence.proof: 1440: the pad is operable in the first viewport. I tapped 'Log reading' empty and got 'Enter a reading before logging it.' I keyed 1 . 0 4 4 and logged it: 'Pre-boil gravity logged: 1.044 SG at 08:45. 0.002 under target, flagged on the record.' The step got a flag icon and the paper record went to '4 of 8 readings · 1 flagged'. I finished with 'Use the sample reading' x4 and got 'Batch 231 record complete.' The values match the static record table further down (12.4 hL, 1.054 SG, 19.0 °C, 10.2 hL), and everything is labelled 'Sample batch. Runs in your browser; nothing is saved.'
evidence.craft: Strong palette and type hierarchy, and the axe list is empty. Defects: at 1440 the paper record under the hero copy is cut by the fold at y=741, so the rows that 'fill in' as you log land below the viewport. A dead block of about 120px sits under the dark pad on the right. The 'Use the sample reading' ghost link is indented out of line with 'Log reading'. The 12px mono labels ('Sample batch. Runs in your browser...', '3 of 8 readings') are small on the dark and white panels. The heavy four-line H1 at 1440 crowds the subhead.
evidence.mobile: 390: recomposed rather than shrunk. The keypad opens inline under the selected step (md:hidden pane), keys are 95x56, and 'Log reading' is full width. After logging, the next step's pad opens and the status line sits at the bottom of the pad, still in view (y=790 of 844). The menu button is 44px+; tapping 'Menu' showed 'Close' with three links plus a CTA, and tapping 'The record' scrolled there and closed the menu. There is no overflow at 390 or 320. Downsides: the paper record sits below the whole pad, and the page runs to 5,481px.
evidence.honesty: Samples are labelled where they appear ('Sample batch...' in the pad header, 'Sample batch record. On a live install the step names, units and target ranges are the brewery's own.', 'Row from the sample record for batch 231.'). No invented customers or numbers, and 'Pricing is not set yet.' But the form says 'No card, no sales call. You hear back by email.' before submit, and after a valid submit it says 'Nothing was sent. Early-access requests are not open yet, and nothing you typed has left this page.' That disclosure comes after the click and contradicts the line above the button.
evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440, 768 and 390 with no console errors. Empty log shows an inline error. Draft input caps at 6 characters ('999999'). The decimal point is ignored when the draft is empty or already has one. 'Change this reading' reopens the step with the value pre-filled. 'Start the sample over' resets to 3 readings with the status 'Sample reset to 08:40...'. The hero CTA anchors to #early-access. An empty form submit triggers native 'Please fill out this field.'. The weak points: the CTA scroll does not move focus to the form (activeElement stayed at the top), and the form's only outcome is the not-sent message.
evidence.copy: Brewhouse-specific and consistent: 'written wet at the kettle, typed up dry in the evening and read a week late', 'An off reading gets flagged, not blocked.', 'Nothing waits on the app.', 'Good fit / Not for / What you get / Cost'. One conversion label is used everywhere. Weak spot: 'You hear back by email' promises a response the form cannot deliver.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: promise, CTA with microcopy, an operable sample pad and the top of the filling record are all in one viewport. 390: headline, subhead, full-width CTA, 'Email and brewery name. No card, no sales call.' and the pad header with its sample label are in view, but the keypad itself starts below the fold. The CTA label is consistent, but what it leads to (a form that does not send) is not stated in view.

problems: The early-access form promises 'You hear back by email' and only reveals 'Nothing was sent... requests are not open yet' after a valid submit; the disclosure is late and contradicts the copy above it.
At 1440 the paper batch record that fills as you log sits under the hero copy, cut by the fold, so the main feedback of the demo lands off-screen. At 390 the record sits below the whole pad.

Small execution lapses: the 12px mono labels on the dark pad, the misaligned 'Use the sample reading' ghost link, dead space under the pad at 1440, and the CTA anchor that does not move focus into the form.

reason: B shows the product doing its job: a brewer can tap a gravity into a big-key tablet pad, watch it get flagged and see the owner's record fill, all in the first screen and recomposed properly for the phone. A has better-written prose but only a static list, and its primary action mails an address the brief never gave. I would switch only if B's after-the-click 'Nothing was sent' disclosure were judged worse than A's invented email destination.
